name: Adenosine (topical hair)

lead: Topical adenosine is an ingredient in hair-growth cosmetics, used by people hoping to thicken thinning hair.

It acts on dermal papilla cells, the follicle's signalling centre: a 2012 study in cultured mouse whisker follicles found it raised FGF-2 and FGF-7, stimulated dermal papilla growth and lengthened the growth phase. A 2024 paper found the androgen receptor pathway to be a candidate target, separate from minoxidil's mechanism. The work is laboratory-based.

paras: It is applied to the scalp as a leave-on serum or tonic in a daily routine, and is sometimes used next to other hair treatments. Hair changes are generally judged over months.
It is sold as a cosmetic ingredient, and safety data were not covered in the sources reviewed. Human trial results for this use were not found.

angle.text: Topical adenosine is used for thicker-looking hair: it acts on dermal papilla cells and lengthens the growth phase in lab studies. The research so far is in cultured cells and follicles.

lead: Adenosine is a naturally occurring nucleoside used as a cosmetic active in hair-growth products. Laboratory work reports that it acts on dermal papilla cells, the follicle's signalling center. [1][2]

A 2012 study in cultured mouse whisker follicles found that adenosine stimulated dermal papilla growth and lengthened the anagen (growth) phase by raising cysteine levels through fibroblast growth factors 2 and 7. [1] A 2024 paper examined an adenosine complex's effects on gene expression in dermal papilla cells and identified the androgen receptor pathway as a candidate target, distinct from minoxidil's mechanism. [2]
infobox: FGF-mediated dermal papilla stimulation; AR pathway inhibition [1][2]

paras: In the mouse follicle culture, adenosine increased the expression of FGF-2 and FGF-7 in dermal papilla and extended anagen. [1] The 2024 paper reports that adenosine complexes inhibit androgen receptor signalling, comparing gene-expression changes against minoxidil. [2]

Evidence in the sources reviewed is mainly laboratory based. The 2024 paper is titled as concerning male and female patterned hair loss, but no randomized controlled trial of topical adenosine was available to summarise here. [2]

timeline.event: Mouse vibrissae organ-culture study on adenosine and dermal papilla published. [1]
Study of adenosine complex and AR signalling published. [2]
